scores.visual_critic_note: The UI chrome is clean — decent typographic hierarchy, intentional muted earth-tone palette for the circle groups — but the main visualization is cut off below the viewport, the dark navy edge bundles create muddy noise against the translucent circles, and the overall composition feels unfinished rather than designed.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: scaleSqrt correctly used for circle-size encoding in force layout; pack layout uses D3's built-in area-correct algorithm; domains are data-driven via d3.extent; key functions present for object constancy; no bar/area baseline, dual-axis, or line-gap issues apply to this structural topology visualization.
scores.stress_test_note: Tension slider correctly uses RAF coalescing, but easing-param sliders fire full updateLayout() on every input with no debounce (update storm), layout switching never calls .interrupt() before creating a new transition (relying solely on D3's implicit preemption), and hover/click handlers carry no touch-event filtering against double-trigger on mobile.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Single-view design with strong interaction (highlight/fade, toggleable links, tension slider) manages 200 nodes and 300 bundled edges well, but the default circle-pack state renders a dense tangle of crossing bundles at the center and 8 layout buttons upfront impose immediate decision overhead before the viewer can read the data.

proposer: Inlined the three event handler functions (`onMouseOver`, `onMouseOut`, `onClick`) directly into the `.on()` chain, reducing ~27 lines to ~10. Used `clearHighlights()` in mouseout instead of duplicating its logic. Behavior is preserved: hover highlights leaves/shallow parents, click selects/deselects with fade, mouseout clears when no selection active.
